Prometheus alerting rules: "Alerting rules without the `keep_firing_for` clause will deactivate on the first evaluation where the condition is not met." Operators: "`vector1 and vector2` results in a vector consisting of the elements of `vector1` for which there are elements in `vector2` with exactly matching label sets. Other elements are dropped." The rule has no keep_firing_for.

incident-drill.sh L39-41 `load() { while [ ! -f "$work/stop" ]; do read_products 50 10 >> "$work/codes"; done }`, L44-45 `load &` / `load_pid=$!`; L107 `touch "$work/stop"`, L108 `wait "$load_pid"`. L4 `set -euo pipefail`, last line L117 `above "$hour"` (awk `exit !(v > t)`) → non-zero unless 1h share > 0.0672. Runbook L5-6 cites the drill.

Prometheus querying basics: range vector selectors "select a range of samples back from the current instant." rate(): "calculates the per-second average rate of increase of the time series in the range vector." So [5m] drops failed requests older than 5 min, [1h] keeps them up to an hour; the captured drill output (5m: no, 1h: yes) agrees.

git-revert DESCRIPTION: "Given one or more existing commits, revert the changes that the related patches introduce, and record some new commits that record them." A recorded commit can itself be reverted. staging Application syncs from envs/staging of the config repo (apps/staging.yaml).

Repo inspection: envs/staging/migrate-hook.yaml is an Argo CD `hook: Sync` Pod running the donhang-migrate bundle ("Always the same tag as the api"). EF Core docs: "Running this executable applies the migrations contained within it" — an older bundle applies forward only and has no Down for newer migrations; Argo CD only applies manifests. So the applied migration stays after a revert.
